judged_text: Guest emails are persisted and compared with no normalization: the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` and the `attendee.email === user.email` authorization check are both case-sensitive exact matches, so the same address can be added twice in different case and a user whose stored email case differs from the attendee row is not recognized as an attendee. Duplicate attendees accumulate in bookings (duplicate calendar/email sends to the same mailbox), and the isAttendee fallback authorization silently fails for users whose email is stored with different casing, producing inconsistent permission outcomes.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler` the attendee/duplicate logic compares raw email strings without normalization. Authorization uses `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)` (case-sensitive), so a user whose stored email casing differs from the attendee row will not be recognized as an attendee and may be wrongly forbidden. Likewise, duplicate prevention uses `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` (also case-sensitive), allowing the same mailbox to be added multiple times with different casing, which then persists via `attendees.createMany` and can lead to duplicate attendee rows and duplicate downstream calendar/email updates. The blacklist check is also inconsistent because `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased but `guest` is not lowercased before `includes`.
